internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across 37 of 38 occurrences the root names a human being as one discrete individual — a man (imru', al-mar', or the bare masculine imra' in 19:28 'a man of evil') or a woman (imra'a). It is never a collective 'mankind/men/women'; plurality shows only as duals (imra'atayn 28:23, imra'ataan 2:282) or as distributive 'every individual' (kullu imri'in). 'Wife' is not a meaning of the word: imra'a means 'wife' only when bound to a male (imra'atu fir'awn, imra'atuhu), and stays plain 'woman' when unbound (the ruling woman 27:23, the two women 28:23, the witnessing pair 2:282, the believing woman 33:50, the woman fearing her husband 4:128 who is married yet whose marriage is carried by ba'l, not by imra'a). The single remaining token, marī' at 4:4 ('eat it wholesome and agreeable'), describes palatable food and has no Quran-internal path to 'human individual'; it is a homonymous lexicalized isolate that keeps the whole-root claim from being STRONG or universal.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: The root does NOT entail: (1) collective humanity/species (that is insaan/bashar/naas — this root has no native plural); (2) a spouse/marital bond — 2:102 sets 'between al-mar' and his zawj', distinguishing the individual from the pairing-relation, and 4:128 pairs imra'a with ba'l ('her husband'), so 'wife' is annexation-supplied, not lexical; (3) a default 'a man' role — 2:282 uses rajul for the man and this root only for the women, and the masculine of this root leans to 'each/the individual'; (4) any moral or qualitative loading — used of the condemned (111:4) and the righteous (66:11, 3:35) alike; (5) any eventive/verbal content (zero verbs); (6) bidirectionally, the person-family never means 'wholesome' and marī' (4:4) never denotes a person.

Rejected on Quran-internal grounds: the one marī' token is about food, offering no internal bridge to personhood; such an abstraction fits everything and violates the narrowest-account mandate; and positing it requires importing external lexical etymology (muru'a-type reasoning) barred by the source policy. internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently sort the 38 tokens into the same structure and converge on the same grade. (1) The nominal family (37 tokens) is internally bridged: 19:28 «ٱمْرَأَ سَوْءٍ» shows the tā'-less masculine base predicated of a father, sitting beside feminine imra'a-t, proving imru'/imra'a is one gender-inflected lexeme, and the kalaala legal frame uses masculine imru' (4:176) and feminine imra'a (4:12) for the same decedent role. (2) The feminine 'wife'-vs-'woman' split is exceptionless and syntactically conditioned (annexation to a male → 'wife'; unbound → 'woman'), a clean sub-result rather than a resistance. (3) marī' (4:4) is an ADJ in a disjoint semantic field with no internal bridge — a resistant lexicalized class. Per contract, a resistant lexicalized sub-class caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE; additionally the 'root contribution' is a frozen, verbless nominal 'person' whose strongest unifying nuance (individuation/accountability) co-varies with kull/bayna/eschatological yawma and is undercut by the flat narrative 19:28, so it is held as nuance, not core. Quran-internally there is no path from 'wholesome-to-consume' to 'a human individual'; bridging it would require external lexical etymology barred by source policy. resistant_deep_analysis.preliminary_note: The lone ADJ token, faʿīl pattern, paired with hanī' (root hn') describing palatable consumption of the sadaqaat. Quran-internally there is no path from 'wholesome-to-consume' to 'a human individual'; bridging it would require external lexical etymology barred by source policy. It is therefore an unbridged, homonymous/lexicalized isolate on the same consonantal skeleton — a resistant class distinct from the nominal person-family.
resistant_deep_analysis.reconciliation_rationale: No Quran-internal occurrence links palatability to personhood; unifying would require barred external etymology. It is held as a separate unbridged lexicalized class, capping the whole-root grade at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) each partitioned the 38 tokens identically into person-family (37) plus marī' (1) and each proposed MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE for the whole root, converging without coordination.
candidate_root_contribution: For the nominal family (37/38 tokens) the root م ر أ contributes 'a single, countable, individuated adult human person' — inherently singular/dual (never a native plural; the collective is suppleted by naas/nisaa'/rijaal), gender-marked by morphology (masc. imru'/al-mar'/imra' 'a/the man, the individual'; fem. imra'a 'a woman'), and inherently neutral in quality. The feminine specializes to 'wife' only under annexation/possessive to a male (construct or pronoun), never lexically; the masculine never reciprocally specializes to 'husband'. There is NO verbal/eventive realization of this root in the corpus. The 38th token, the adjective marī' (4:4), denotes 'wholesome/agreeable to consume' and is a separate, Quran-internally unbridged lexicalized class, not covered by this contribution.
